issues.subject: Grid & Gutter: the index page comes back
issues.text:
GRID & GUTTER
Five links and one long read. Tuesday {date}

View in your browser: https://gridandgutter.example/issues/grid-and-gutter-the-index-page-comes-back

Morning. A short one this week because I spent the weekend at Shoreditch Type Weekend, which is on again this Saturday 24 October if you missed the first round (tickets were still at £18 last night). The theme that kept coming up there is this week's long read: plain lists of everything a site has, sorted, with no cleverness.

THE LONG READ

The index page comes back
Tobias Wren, Margin Notes, 14 min
Wren looks at eleven cultural sites relaunched in the past year and finds that seven of them shipped an A to Z index of every page, often linked from the footer and used more than the main navigation. His argument is that search taught people to scan, and an index is a search result you can see all at once. The section on how the Rijkhaven archive sorted 4,000 object pages by maker surname is worth the time on its own.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/the-index-page-comes-back

FIVE LINKS

Wayfinding for a museum with no front door
Studio Kade on signing a building with four entrances of equal weight. Lots of photos of the cardboard prototypes.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/wayfinding-for-a-museum-with-no-front-door

An icon audit spreadsheet you can copy
Columns for name, metaphor, stroke weight, sizes in use and the screens each one appears on. Dull and useful.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/an-icon-audit-spreadsheet-you-can-copy

Interview: the person who designs the council's forms
Eighteen years of making forms for a London borough, and why she has never once used a placeholder as a label.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/interview-the-person-who-designs-the-council-s-forms

1970s rail timetables, scanned
A volunteer archive of regional timetables, all set by hand in two weights. The density is a lesson for anyone building tables.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/1970s-rail-timetables-scanned

Talk: dense tables that people can still read
Forty minutes from Ana Liddell at last month's Interface North. Skip to 19:30 for the bit on zebra striping.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/talk-dense-tables-that-people-can-still-read

That's it for this week. If you're at the type weekend on Saturday, I'll be at the letterpress table around noon.

Maren

--

issues.subject: Grid & Gutter: why every dashboard looks the same
issues.text:
GRID & GUTTER
Five links and one long read. Tuesday {date}

View in your browser: https://gridandgutter.example/issues/grid-and-gutter-why-every-dashboard-looks-the-same

Morning. This week's long read made me look at four of my own projects with some embarrassment. The links are a mixed bag, as usual, with one very good piece on handwriting in signage.

THE LONG READ

Why every dashboard looks the same
Priscilla Dunmore, Field Report, 11 min
Dunmore traces the four-cards-then-a-line-chart layout back to a handful of admin templates sold around 2016 and argues that most teams never asked what their users check first. She rebuilds a logistics dashboard around the one question its operators ask every morning (what is late) and the result is mostly a sorted list.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/why-every-dashboard-looks-the-same

FIVE LINKS

Handwritten signs in hospital corridors
A photo essay on the notes staff tape over official signage, and what they say about the signs underneath.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/handwritten-signs-in-hospital-corridors

A colour contrast checker that shows you the failures in context
Paste a palette, get every text and background pair it allows, with the failing ones crossed out.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/a-colour-contrast-checker-that-shows-you-the-failures-in

The case for fewer breakpoints
A studio in Leeds went from seven breakpoints to three and wrote up what broke. Less than they expected.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/the-case-for-fewer-breakpoints

Bus stop flags of Europe
Someone has photographed bus stop signs in 60 cities. The Scandinavian ones are as calm as you would hope.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/bus-stop-flags-of-europe

Design review checklists, collected
Twelve teams shared the checklists they use before a design goes to build. Several have a line for 'what happens when this is empty'.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/design-review-checklists-collected

See you next Tuesday.

Maren

--

issues.subject: Grid & Gutter: colour systems that survive a rebrand
issues.text:
GRID & GUTTER
Five links and one long read. Tuesday {date}

View in your browser: https://gridandgutter.example/issues/grid-and-gutter-colour-systems-that-survive-a-rebrand

Morning. Three readers sent me this week's long read within an hour of it going up, so I assume some of you have already seen it. Read it again anyway; the second half is the useful part.

THE LONG READ

Colour systems that survive a rebrand
Imogen Saxby, Studio Notes, 16 min
Saxby has led two rebrands at a bank and one at a train operator, and in each case the product colours outlasted the brand that made them. Her rule is to name colours by job (surface, text, warning) and never by hue, so that the brand team can change the hue and nothing in the product has to be renamed. She includes the token list from the train operator, all 41 of them.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/colour-systems-that-survive-a-rebrand

FIVE LINKS

Paper sizes, explained properly
Why A4 is the shape it is, with a diagram that finally made the root-two thing click for me.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/paper-sizes-explained-properly

A free variable font for timetables
Tabular figures by default, a narrow width for platform numbers. Released under the OFL.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/a-free-variable-font-for-timetables

What a museum learned from removing its carousel
Visits to exhibition pages went up a fifth. The carousel had been showing the same three things for two years.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/what-a-museum-learned-from-removing-its-carousel

Annotated screenshots of good settings pages
Thirty settings screens with notes on grouping and wording. A good thing to have open when you are writing labels.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/annotated-screenshots-of-good-settings-pages

The grid behind a 1962 exhibition catalogue
A designer reverse-engineers a Swiss catalogue page by page and overlays the grid. Satisfying.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/the-grid-behind-a-1962-exhibition-catalogue

Until next week.

Maren

--

issues.subject: Grid & Gutter: notes on empty states
issues.text:
GRID & GUTTER
Five links and one long read. Tuesday {date}

View in your browser: https://gridandgutter.example/issues/grid-and-gutter-notes-on-empty-states

Morning. Empty states this week: the screens nobody designs until someone files a bug about them. The links wander off into maps and type.

THE LONG READ

Notes on empty states
Rafael Okonjo, Small Screens, 9 min
Okonjo sorts empty states into three kinds: first use, cleared by the user, and nothing matched. He argues that only the first deserves an illustration and the other two should say plainly what happened and what to do next. The examples from a banking app, where 'no transactions' was shown during an outage, are a good warning.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/notes-on-empty-states

FIVE LINKS

The Ordnance Survey's lettering rules, 1938
A scanned rulebook for hand-lettering maps, including how far a river name may be spaced out.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/the-ordnance-survey-s-lettering-rules-1938

How a newsroom chose its byline size
Six weeks of argument summarised in one chart.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/how-a-newsroom-chose-its-byline-size

Free course: writing for interfaces
Eight short lessons from a content designer at a building society. No sign-up needed.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/free-course-writing-for-interfaces

Loading states that tell you something
A gallery of progress indicators that say what is actually happening, not just that something is.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/loading-states-that-tell-you-something

A type specimen made from bus tickets
An art school project that has no business being this good.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/a-type-specimen-made-from-bus-tickets

Thanks for reading.

Maren

issues.subject: Grid & Gutter: grids for screens that keep changing size
issues.text:
GRID & GUTTER
Five links and one long read. Tuesday {date}

View in your browser: https://gridandgutter.example/issues/grid-and-gutter-grids-for-screens-that-keep-changing-size

Morning. One long read about layout and five links, one of which is a very long video about a single typeface. You have been warned.

THE LONG READ

Grids for screens that keep changing size
Hana Voss, Measure, 13 min
Voss argues that a column grid set at fixed breakpoints is the wrong tool for screens that are resized all day, and proposes grids defined by content width instead: a reading column, a gutter, and whatever space is left. She shows the system on a news site, a settings page and an email client, and the email client is the most convincing of the three.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/grids-for-screens-that-keep-changing-size

FIVE LINKS

Two hours on one typeface
A video essay on a 1950s grotesque, its revivals and the arguments about its lowercase g.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/two-hours-on-one-typeface

Signage at a Danish ferry terminal
Big type, two colours, no icons that need explaining.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/signage-at-a-danish-ferry-terminal

What we learned from a year of design critiques
A product team kept notes on every critique for a year. Most feedback was about copy, not layout.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/what-we-learned-from-a-year-of-design-critiques

A better way to show a date range
Short post, one good idea: drop the repeated month and year when they match.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/a-better-way-to-show-a-date-range

Pattern library for public services
Version 6 is out, with a new pattern for asking about a person's name that does not assume it has two parts.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/pattern-library-for-public-services

Until next Tuesday.

Maren

--

issues.subject: Grid & Gutter: typesetting numbers
issues.text:
GRID & GUTTER
Five links and one long read. Tuesday {date}

View in your browser: https://gridandgutter.example/issues/grid-and-gutter-typesetting-numbers

Morning. This week is about figures, the kind in tables and prices. If you have ever seen a total jump sideways as it updated, the long read is for you.

THE LONG READ

Typesetting numbers
Wendell Achebe, The Proof, 12 min
Achebe walks through tabular and proportional figures, lining and old-style, and when each belongs on a screen. The part on prices is the most practical: align by the decimal point, keep the currency sign out of the column, and never let a live total change width. There is a short table of common UI fonts and which figure styles they ship.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/typesetting-numbers

FIVE LINKS

Receipts as a design object
A collection of shop receipts from 30 countries. The Japanese ones fit an astonishing amount onto 58mm of paper.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/receipts-as-a-design-object

Microcopy for errors, rewritten
Before-and-after pairs from a utility company's app. 'An error occurred' becomes something you can act on.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/microcopy-for-errors-rewritten

A free icon set drawn on a 20px grid
Two hundred icons, one stroke weight, sensible names.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/a-free-icon-set-drawn-on-a-20px-grid

How a charity redesigned its donate page
Fewer choices, one default amount, a clear monthly option. Donations up, complaints down.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/how-a-charity-redesigned-its-donate-page

Letterforms in railway station tiles
Photographs of station names set in ceramic, mostly from the 1900s. Lovely spacing.

Read: https://gridandgutter.example/out/letterforms-in-railway-station-tiles

Back next week.

Maren

--
